title: Knowledge check — 8 questions
note: Unlocks after the applied activity is submitted. Retakes are free and unlimited.

questions.prompt: What makes a "recommend" tier real rather than nominal?
options: That a human signs off on every recommendation
That declining a recommendation is normal — if reviewers accept 99% of them, it is an automated decision with a signature step
That the recommendation includes a confidence score
That the recommendation is logged before the decision is made
questions.explanation: A signature step isn't a gate. The test is whether refusal actually happens, which is the same test Module 3 applies to the human gate in its eight questions.

questions.prompt: What is the axis that sorts decisions into the three tiers?
options: The stakes attached to the decision
How difficult the decision is
Whether the decision requires judgment whose absence nobody would notice
How many people the decision affects
questions.explanation: High-stakes and difficult decisions attract supervision precisely because they are frightening. The danger concentrates where a fluent, wrong output gets filed without comment. Module 1's detection-latency argument arriving as an ethical criterion.

questions.prompt: Which Article 26 duty is a configuration setting you can check today? `[V]`
options: Managing input data for representativeness
Following the provider's instructions for use
Keeping logs for at least six months — a retention period somebody sets, where the common default of 30 or 90 days is probably already wrong
Notifying authorities of serious incidents
questions.explanation: The module calls it the single most actionable sentence in it, because the fix takes minutes and the default is usually non-compliant for high-risk uses.

questions.prompt: What does "these obligations can't be contracted away" mean for procurement? `[V]`
options: That vendor contracts cannot include indemnities for AI failures
That an indemnity allocates who bears the cost of a failure but does not move the duty — so indemnity is not compliance
That deployers must renegotiate all existing AI contracts
That the provider and deployer share obligations equally
questions.explanation: You can negotiate who pays. You can't negotiate away the requirement to have assigned competent human oversight.

options: That the entire EU AI Act was deferred to December 2027

That Annex III employment obligations moved to 2 December 2027 while Article 50's transparency duties were not deferred and became enforceable on 2 August 2026 — catching any organization that runs a chatbot, even one with no high-risk AI
That Article 50 was deferred while high-risk obligations took effect on schedule
That the deferral applies only to organizations headquartered in the EU
questions.explanation: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 entered into force 27 July 2026 and moved the high-risk date. Article 50 was left out of the deferral. Expect colleagues to be wrong in both directions, and check against a primary source.

questions.prompt: How should the May 2026 privilege ruling in *Mobley* be stated? `[V]`
options: As establishing that AI bias-testing data is privileged

As a denial of a motion to compel on these facts, where privilege applied because the vendor's attorneys curated the analysis and used its results in providing legal advice — so the structure determines the protection
As holding that bias testing is discoverable in all circumstances
As unrelated to employers, since it concerned a vendor's own data
questions.explanation: Which produces the actionable version: involve counsel *before* you run testing, not after somebody asks for it. The same analysis run as an HR operational exercise may have entirely different discovery consequences.

questions.prompt: When does German co-determination require works-council involvement in an AI deployment? `[V]`
options: At launch, as a notification
At the planning stage, under §90 — with §80(3) presuming an employer-funded external expert, and §95 reaching AI-established selection criteria
Only where the system makes automated decisions without human review
Only in organizations above a headcount threshold
questions.explanation: Which makes consultation a dependency with a lead time on the project plan rather than a message sent at go-live. Note the boundary: a labour court held that merely permitting a browser-based AI tool didn't trigger co-determination: the question is what the system does inside your estate.

questions.prompt: Which of the four rules colliding on your AI logs overrides the others?
options: Your organization's retention schedule, since it is the organization's own policy
Article 26's six-month minimum
A legal hold, which requires preservation from the moment litigation is reasonably anticipated — and which cannot reach a system nobody told legal about
The vendor's default configuration
questions.explanation: Which is why the module says telling your legal team the system exists and generates records is frequently the most valuable sentence in the exercise. The medical-information complication sits on top of all four.
